review_text: I ordered this watchband in hopes of it really being made of leather. As one who previously had a career in the Leather craft industry, I have an affinity for products made of real leather. When I first saw the actual band, I honestly had trouble, based on the look, telling if the band was real leather or not. It definitely smelled like leather; but I have smelled simulated leather scent that smells like real leather. So, I didn’t base my assessment on how the band initially smelled. After, several weeks of daily wear, I have come to believe this watch band is leather, at least the top of the band. The liner layer of the underside is likely not leather. The part I believe to be leather may be leather (cow/animal hide) derived from a rough (suede) cut with a sealing layer or coat or material (some times a mix of color, sealant, and adhesive) that works to smooth, color, seal, and give a grain (the natural pattern of hide after hair removal and curing) look to sueded (a slice of hide cut/split from the grain layer of hide). Conversely, it may be grain layer leather that has had a thickened color/sealing coat. Additionally, it still smells of leather and has proved itself to be very durable.This watchband reminds me more and more of the band I loved and had for years and years on my beloved Timex Sport.Bottom line: I am very happy with this watchband and gladly recommend it to anyone wanting a durable, comfortable, leather wristband.

product_name: AEG HX6-30STM Handstaubsauger / ca. 30 min Laufzeit / 2 Leistungsstufen / Zubehör / ausziehbare Fugendüse / 500 ml / intelligente Ladeabschaltung / Doppelfilterung / Ladekontrollanzeige / petrol
review_header: Hier wurden Probleme gelöst die noch gar nicht da waren…
review_text: ► VORTEILE ◄ ✅ Saugleistung ✅ Verarbeitung ✅ Rollen erleichtern Umgang ✅ Saugrüssel erweiterbar ✅ Filter leicht zu reinigen ► NACHTEILE ◄ ❌ nur an Ladestation ladbar ► FAZIT ◄ Mir hat besonders gut der leichte Umgang mit dem Handstaubsauger gefallen. Die Rollen die leichtgängig sind erleichtert die Führung über alle Flächen. Außerdem positiv aufgefallen ist mir der Filter welcher, mit einem speziellen Zugmechanismus sich leicht ausklopfen lässt. Etwas sauer aufgestoßen ist mir, dass man nur an der Ladestation laden kann. Kabel reinstecken und Laden ist daher nicht möglich. _____________________________________________________________________ _____________________________________________________________________ ⊲ Erster Eindruck / Verpackung ⊳ Die Verpackung macht auf den ersten Blick echt was her. Seit längerem wählt AEG eine schlichte und im Design dunkel gehaltenen Verpackung für Elektrogeräte. Gefällt mir sehr gut und würde sich zum Beispiel auch als Einweihungsgeschenk in eine neue Wohnung gut eignen. Nimmt man den Staubsauger nun aus der Verpackung merkt man er hat ein angenehmes Gewicht und wirkt solide verarbeitet. Die Oberfläche ist Hochglanz und hat leicht glitzernde Elemente verarbeitet. Nach kurzer Zeit sind Kratzer vorhanden und die Hochglanz Oberfläche nicht mehr so strahlend. Gut darüber kann man hinweg sehen. Wo ich nicht drüber hinweg sehen kann ist, die Ladestation. Zwar macht die Ladestation alles richtig mit Wandmontage etc. aber mir der Fakt missfallen, dass man den Handstaubsauger ledeglich über die Ladestation laden kann. Hier wäre ein optionaler Anschluss direkt an das Netzteil eine bessere Lösung gewesen. Ansonsten fällt erster Eindruck sehr gut aus und man gewinnt einen guten soliden ersten Eindruck. ⊲ Saugleistung ⊳ Die Saugleistung ist für einen Handstaubsauger ausgesprochen gut und vorzeigbar. Als Einsatztort wurde das Auto gewählt. Normalerweise sauge ich das Auto innen an der Tankstelle da es hier am unkompliziertesten geht. Jetzt bin ich aber umgestiegen, da der Einsatz des HX6 angenehm leicht durchführbar ist. Zwar ist nach etwa 26 Minuten Schluss in normalen Betrieb. Reicht aber für die Reinigung eines Ford Focus Kombi ohne Probleme. Meiner Meinung nach wäre der Einsatzort mit Montage an der Garagenwand am sinnvollsten. Da schnell zur Hand und danke Wandmontage leicht abnehmbar. ⊲ Reinigung ⊳ Wir hatten jetzt bereits mehrere Handstaubsauger auch von namhaften Herstellern und ich muss sagen AEG hat die Reinigung des Behälters sehr gut gelöst. Ein Knopf öffnet den Behälter und mittels Drehverschluss kann der Filter entnommen werden. Der Filter hat einen Zugmechanismus, der es erlaubt durchhochziehen und loslassen schnell den Filter zu reinigen. Funktioniert alles sehr unkompliziert und intuitiv. Ich kann mir aber vorstellen, dass dieser Zugmechanismus bei unsachgemäßer Benützung beschädigt werden kann. Filter kann auch mit Wasser gereinigt werden. Würde ich auf jeden Fall mindesten einmal im Monat durchführen, hängt aber sehr stark mit der Benützung zusammen. ⊲ Benützung ⊳ Der HX6 von AEG ist vorzeigbar. Dank den Rollen an der Vorderseite der Düse ist ein sanftes Gleiten über alle Oberflächen unproblematisch. Rollen sind leichtgängig und bestehen aus Kunststoff. Bei längerer Benützung verfangen sich längere Haare aber leider doch und die Reinigung der Rollen ist etwas fummelig. Ansonsten hat mir der ausziehbare Rüssel gut gefallen. Da Die Vorderseite des HX6 etwas groß ausfällt und daher nicht immer in alle Ritzen kommt, vor allem beim Reinigen des Autos sehr hilfreich. Der Rüssel kann etwa auf eine länge von 12 cm herausgezogen werden. Bei zu hohem Druck vor allem bei Autositzen kann der Rüssel wieder einfahren und die Reinigung behindern. Würde aber meinen das ist meckern auf hohem Niveau. ⊲ abschließende Worte ⊳ Abschließend kann ich sagen, dass der Handstaubsauger von AEG ausgesprochen gut ist. Die leichte Reinigung in Verbund mit den leichtgängigen Rollen an der Vorderseite gefallen mir gut, dass Laden ausschließlich nur an der Ladestation funktioniert ist etwas umständlich. Dennoch konnte ich während dem Gebrauch kaum negativ Punkte finden die einen Sterne-Abzug wert wären. Volle 5 Sterne.

After putting 100 miles on this helmet, I can confidently say it’s a solid choice for riders looking for comfort, protection, and good overall features at a reasonable price.


Fit & Comfort:

The fit is quite good, though I’d note that the shape leans more towards a round profile rather than a long-oval. If you typically wear long-oval helmets, this might feel a little snug on the top of my forehead. That said, once adjusted properly, it sits comfortably without pressure points, and I had no issues with fatigue after extended rides.


Features & Performance:

Ventilation: The airflow is decent, helping to keep things cool even on warmer days.

Visor & Visibility: The visor mechanism works smoothly, and visibility is excellent, giving a wide field of view without obstruction.

Noise Levels: As with most helmets in this price range, there is some wind noise at higher speeds, but it’s nothing excessive or unbearable.

Overall Verdict:

For the price, this helmet offers a great balance of comfort, protection, and practical features. If your head shape leans more toward round rather than long-oval, it should be a great fit. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a quality helmet without breaking the bank.

A craft that goes back for centuries, as was explained to me at L'Occitane a few years back. French milled is really the original organic which is probably why it's making a comeback. No chemicals. Natural oils for scent & remedy. Natural fats for moisturizing, in this case Shea . Because of this process you get thick foaming suds in the shower & SOFT skin out of the shower. I've never used Pre's soap but, every bar of French milled I have used lasts forever bc of the process & this bar is huge. To the Lemongrass scent, reminds me of citronella. Not the mass produced, genetically modified stuff out there . Real citronella if you've smelled it as an oil, is lemony & tart & clean. It can be intoxicating if it's a quality oil. You know the expression that you love something so much you want to bathe in it? Yeah, that was me in the shower with this Lemongrass. Ironically, wasn't bothered by any mosquitos later in the day. I usually only like citrus on my plate but this is something different that won me over. This is a nice gender neutral scent. Great for a gift or a gift to yourself.

review_text:
TLDR: I recommend this brand for everyday use!


Using their size guide we actually got shoes that fit the first time around! If you’ve ever bought shoes online before, especially for kids AND considering European sizes, that’s a small miracle.


We mostly wear them barefoot (without socks), I had a small period of adjusting my outside toe to that as expected (photographed) but now I can with ease, and if I choose a low sock the fit/wear is just as pleasant, no sliding down on the back of heel, there’s actually small cushions on the inside of the shoe I tried to picture. They’re so comfortable. I never tie or untie these, I slide on and off each wear, the sock fit is a very nice feature for me here. I included photos comparing to crocs, vivos, and hey dudes but those all have pretty wide toe boxes.


My girls, ages 5&2 loved them from the get—sparkly and beautiful, and not in a ‘in your face pink glitter for a girl’ color, they can go with or without socks (never experiencing a blister) AND they can take them on and off without help. Which holds a lot of weight for most moms.


Speaking of weight, they’re very light. They don’t feel blocky or sound like my kids are having a hard time wearing them, even with the wider toe box which is my favorite part and is likely why the fit is so comfortable for all of us. Most US made adult tennis shoes have tight toe boxes where these do not, without compromising look/style. I love the tannish beige, I accepted they wouldn’t stay ‘clean’ forever but I don’t regret my choice. They match with everything and I can wear them with every kind of bottom except skinny jeans as I just personally don’t like the look of tight jeans with a tennis shoe but I’ll wear leggings, sweats, joggers and shorts with them.


Lastly, Kids’ tend to show the quality of a shoe/brand pretty quickly. These have held up well as being our main shoe since summer 2024—parks, outside play, coaching volleyball and still nice enough for church. Current (Dec 2024) photos showing wear included.

review_header: These shoes are worth the money
review_text:
I really love these shoes. Did a lot of research and read a lot of reviews. Ordered these because the price was reasonable and the shoes looked to be comfortable for everyday use.

Bought these 8 months ago and wear them 3 to 7 days a week. Wear them to work and I’m on my feet the majority (75-80%) of my day. I have no other boots or shoes for the bike. I walk around festivals and concerts without any fatigue or pain. These shoes are built to last and very comfortable. They have not lost their shape or are fraying. The laces will eventually have to be replaced, but the wear and tear on them are no more than usual. I have rode in weather and the shoes were not overly water resistant, however they did not gather water also. The tread works for dry use, however oil and other liquids do make you slip a little. The size was a bit small for my feet, would recommend getting a size half bigger.

7 months into wearing them I replaced the inserts with some Dr. Scholls work message inserts. I have been enjoying these shoes even more. Replaced them mostly for work, due to being on my feet all the time.

I wear these in Texas heat and they don’t make my feet sweat like crazy (like leather does). During the winter however, they do not keep your feet warm (without the proper socks). Riding in 50 or below weather you will need the proper socks.

Pros:

Comfortable, sturdy, keeps structure, no breakdown or large creasing around the movement areas, Price point

Cons:

Not majorly water resistant and not warm in 40–50-degree weather on a motorcycle, will slip a little when you put your feet in oil, need to go up a half size,

review_text: I bought this to have a means to play CDs, DVDs and VCR tapes in one compact box.  I haven't even used the record function, and probably never will. How about just "On/Off".In short, there are too many hidden/automatic/nonavailable/weirdly labeled things about this that make it awkward to use.  I will probably never buy a combo drive in the future if I can help it, even if I have to hunt down generations-old devices on eBay to get a separate CD player, separate DVD player, and separate VCR. product_name: EVANS Coolant EC53001-EC42001 High Performance Waterless Coolant and Prep Fluid Combo Pack, 2 Gallon
review_header: Less pressure, fewer failures & nothing gets poisoned !
review_text:
I'm running Evans in two Honda Civics with the goal of reducing intra-cooling system pressures.  The Evans alternative to conventional anti-freeze won't boil unless reaches 375F, and, of course if it ever did, you'd already have experienced catastrophic failure...  In normal operation, it creates no steam pressure and thus will not pass thru my 16 psi radiator caps - UNLESS the coolant level is too high in the top of the radiator tank.  While it doesn't create steam pressure, it does create hydraulic pressure, which is to say that the liquid will expand by (they tell me) about 7% when it heats up to say 200F.  If it got filled up to the top of the radiator neck, the expanding fluid will push through the pressure cap and go into the overflow reservoir - from which it will NOT get sucked back by the differential in pressures that moves regular coolant back and forth.  If you did fill up the radiator tank, the Evans will overflow until it finds its own level inside of the radiator top tank.  In the case of my vehicles, one found its level approximately 0.5" below the inner flange of the neck; the other leveled out at about 0.75" below...  (Normally, I run coolant right up to the reservoir overflow tube, so this Evans characteristic was initially puzzling and quite different.)


For my stock performance vehicles - which never heat up unless there has been a systems failure - the merits are as follows... First, I'm hoping that the lack of steam pressure build-up will mean that the cheapo plastic radiator tanks that Honda uses will no longer explode at the seams.  Ditto the coolant hoses.  (Whether multiple previous failures have been due to internal pressure, or expansion-contraction fatigue is uncertain, but I'm confident that the risk of failure using Evans is substantially lower.


Additionally, I like that:  the coolant is non-toxic to pets and it supposedly will never age out and allow internal corrosion.


A bonus on Civics like mine is that those systems only have a cooling system capacity of 1.1 gallons, so the additional cost of running Evans is insignificant, especially when compared to the price of blown head gaskets that can result from cooling system failure.  The merits for motorcycles should be similarly appealing.


On my classic truck powered by a SBC, the merits would be the same but would also include an ability to continue conducting heat out of the motor even if the system spirals up into the anxiety inducing 240-260F range where coolant cavitation can cause internal hot spots that can result in engine failure.  That SBC system uses in excess of 5 gallons of coolant, so I'm waiting for the next coolant change cycle before making the switch, but nevertheless, even at 5 x $45 (plus the prep fluid costs), the cost is modest when compared to the costs of catastrophic engine failure that is more likely to occur when using conventional coolant...


On the conversions that I've done, after the preliminary coolant drain, I opened the heater core valves and removed the engine thermostats and used a small shop vac to blow coolant out of the systems.  I probably ran the shop vac for 30 minutes, but might have gotten by with less time.  Regardless, my subsequent coolant "refractometer" tests showed that I had successfully reduced the water content of the systems below 1% water, which is well below their recommended maximum level of < = 3% water.

review_header: Love these sensors, I keep finding more uses for these. Small and they work great.
review_text: I love these sensors I have been finding more and more uses for them. They have helped identify some areas in the house that needed attention where the air is stagnant or we have higher humidity. Got these to expand on our current setup and I cant say enough good about them to be honest. They are small, easy to use, set up and are surprisingly accurate for being so small. You can hang them from the thin strap they come with or attach them with velcro as I have done in certain areas. The batteries really do last about two years, I just last month had to replace batteries on other sensors I have had but I will say the wifi sensor has gotten smaller in this time which I love. You can plug in the wifi sensor this one comes with and still have space for the other plug which my old did not. The app is great and easy to use and provides you with several different functions and shows you trends and changes that you can go back and track along with real live time temperature and humidity. I have used these in our attic, the kids room and even in a cooler to make sure the temp didn't get too high. I have them around the house, garage on the porch, pantry and just keep finding uses for these. I have used Govee items in the past and these are made well and work well just like the other products I have used from this company. Overall I am really happy with these and will most likely be adding more to our set up still.

product_name: The Cat's Table
review_text: Michael Ondaatje has written an excellent novel which, although he says in the author's note is entirely fictional, seems to be steeped in autobiographical nostalgia. He even uses his own name, Michael, for the narrator - the book is written in the first person except for the intriguing prologue where it is almost as if the adult Michael Ondaatje is looking back at the boy he once was, embarking on the adventure of a long sea voyage. I am sure Michael Ondaatje did, indeed, sail back from India on a ship like the 'Oronsay', and probably met some pretty original characters. They may or may not have been direct inspirations for this novel, but whatever the origins of 'The Cat's Table', this novel is a stand-out story.The mischievous innocence of young boys travelling on their own from India to England to go to an English school is superbly drawn and entirely convincing. The characters they encounter on board ship are larger than life and twice as interesting, varying from a circus acrobat to jazz-loving, eccentric Mr Mazappa, from the lonely teacher, Mr Fonseca, to the enigmatic Miss Lasqueti (who turns out to be something quite other than she first appeared). The oddities of activities add a fairy-tale quality to the story and sometimes the effect is almost like 'Alice in Wonderland'. The picaresque quality of this 'in media res' tale - three boys caught in the middle place between stages in their lives, trying to make sense of the world around them, but captured in the warp of the mini-world of the ship's confines - is an ideal opportunity for a novelist's imagination to wander at will. And Michael Ondaatje does wander, to great effect.The 'Cat's Table', socially the bottom table on the ship, the other end of the scale from the Captain's Table, creates an ideal space from which to develop this unusual tale. But Michael Ondaajte does not just tell the story of the boat trip. He balances the lively narrative with a deep and often profound insight into the mental development of Michael's character, a boy on the cusp of puberty, just about to grow out of childhood. Sensitivity of language and feeling is one of Ondaatje's strengths and he plays it for all it's worth in this magical book.The chapters are short, the characters luminous, the escapades entertaining, and the whole book leaves a satisfying sense of a well-written, very readable novel. I highly recommend this book to readers. You won't be disappointed.

review_text: I've kept various aquariums over the last 30 years and periodically I have battled the dreaded blue green slime algae. Spoiler alert: the algae ALWAYS wins. When the algae made its appearance in my 20 gallon tank this January I was crushed. I began removing it by hand every other day. It was disgusting and the smell... if you've had this algae you know the smell I am talking about. Even removing as much as I could by hand within 48 hours it looked like I hadn't done anything at all. Google came to the rescue and I found out about this product. I was skeptical because I couldn't find anything about what the ingredients are. Just that it's not an antibiotic (this is actually cyanobacteria and traditionally fishkeepers would treat with antibiotics back in the day) and is safe for fish, shrimp, and plants. I decided I didn't have anything to lose and gave it a shot. I added the first dose and noticed the next day that the algae didn't appear quite as green. product_name: Energy 5.1 Take Classic Home Theater System (Set of Six, Black)
review_header: Did a ton of research and read a lot of glowing reviews about this set before ordering, and I have to say I'm very impressed!
review_text: Did a ton of research and read a lot of glowing reviews about this set before ordering, and I have to say I'm very impressed and happy!This set replaces the 7.1 speakers which came with my Onkyo home theater in a box which you can see here: https://www.amazon.com/Onkyo-SKS-HT540-Channel-Theater-Speaker/dp/B000GU78Z4?ie=UTF8&SubscriptionId=AKIAJ3NOW7JKGQLTEY4A&camp=2025&creative=165953&creativeASIN=B000GU78Z4&linkCode=xm2&tag=cnet-api-20.My pre-HDMI, 10 year old Onkyo receiver is still doing fine, but I've never really been 100% satisfied with the speakers which were packaged with it. The Energy 5.1 Take Classic 5.1 system is AMAZING to my critical ears! The 4 small satellites are all identical, so you know the sound coming from the rear will be every bit as bright and full as the front. The Onkyo satellites, while larger, and seemingly more capable in appearance, were muddy by comparison. The Onkyo surrounds had only a single speaker, so background sounds were limited to whatever that midrange cone could muster.The center speaker contains the same driver array as the satellites, but has two forward facing ports instead of a single rear facing port like the satellites have. This allows more dynamic range pushing forward where dialog and most of your movie's sound will come from. All the Energy satellites have a clear and bright presence.Although this 5.1 system replaces a 7.1 setup, I don't miss the extra 2 rears one bit. The two Energy surround satellites have much more rear presence than the four larger Onkyo surrounds ever did. I no longer have to walk over to the surrounds to confirm they're doing anything. I'm hearing incidental music and effects from the rear I never heard before! In the beginning in Monsters Inc, where we're first brought into the company's front door, in between the characters' conversations, I can hear the unmistakable sound of the building's air conditioning system in the background! Something I never knew was there before! I have to watch all my old favorite movies and experience them all over again!The bass speaker is the real star of the show here. My living room is about 18 feet by 16 feet and opens into the dining area, which then turns a corner into the kitchen, so the Energy speakers have a lot of floor to cover and air to fill. Don't let the fact that the bass has an eight inch down firing speaker fool you. This baby rocks the entire house! It's smaller than the Onkyo bass it replaced, but never have I had such satisfying, deep tones and surprisingly full rumbles coming from my movies before getting the Energy system! Whether it's the mighty, slow-motion on screen progression of a Star Wars battleship, or the ultimate deep bass of my favorite tunes, this diminutive bass speaker is an absolute delight to have in the home. Deep, deep bass can be heard throughout my 1200 square foot home - again, something I've never had before, and something I thought would require spending 3 times or more the price.It took only a few minutes to set up the Energy speakers since I already had the room wired from the previous set. The Onkyo receiver allows me to manually tune volume for each speaker - no automatic mic system here. The Onkyo receiver's speaker calibration allows speaker settings from 1 to 12. I kept all the smaller cubes at 9 and had to lower the bass from the previous set's setting of 10 down to 9. I then had to lower the treble from 8 to 6 and kept the bass at 4. I then adjusted the Energy bass low pass filter knob between 90 and 100hz. This seemed an optimal balance between the bass and the satellites. Too much higher and vocals start sounding a little boomy. I set the Energy bass level knob to 7 (out of 12 - so I guess Onkyo isn't alone with using "12" as a maximum speaker calibration) which gives me just enough punch and boom without exaggerating the bass. If you wanted to pump this puppy up because you want to rattle the windows, go right ahead and crank it to 12! I tend to like a more balanced setting which only shows its surprising deep ends when the music or the movie calls for it. I keep the bass power on automatic. Its little blue front facing LED light stays on during use, and turns off after about 15 minutes or so of sensing no sound being sensed. I have it sitting about a foot from the left front corner of my living room. It's tucked behind the side couch's end table, so I'm not bothered by the blue light (as some have complained here).I would absolutely recommend the Energy 5.1 Take Classic system to anyone with a receiver and critical ear. Your music will finally satisfy you and your movies will surprise you. Take the time to adjust the setup correctly. There is some crucial knob turning on the bass module to balance with whatever settings your receiver allows. You'll be getting up and down from your couch quite a few times during the first few days to make slight adjustments - this is to be expected with any new system, but the rewards are definitely there. Energy's manual recommends a break-in period where they suggest playing wide dynamic music at normal listening levels throughout the first 50 hours. While I understand the need (speakers are moving objects whose glue, mounts, and foam will change their shape, and thus their sound, somewhat as they loosen up after first being used), I would say you'd be fine just playing them as often as you can in the first few days. If you have a very critical ear, you may find the need to make a few more adjustments during and after the break-in period completes. Again, this is normal. I could not be happier with my purchase, and highly recommend this speaker system to anyone with a love for excellent sound.

review_text: I got this Warmies sea turtle on January 5 2024 and have slept with it pretty much every night since. The weight and heat are soothing and the fluffy texture of the body and limbs is wonderful! I already had a Warmies alligator (which I still use), but I got Shelby because I wanted something with concentrated weight. I have terrible period pains and have found that this does a good job of helping to ease them. I like to heat mine up for 70 seconds so it's pretty hot when it comes out of the microwave, but the heat lasts for quite a while and it's easy for me to heat it up again once it does cool down. Sometimes if I need a higher heat I'll put Shelby on top of my heat pad and let the weight keep the heat exactly where I need it. I find the scent to be pleasant, though I will say that I can usually smell the flax a bit more than the lavender. After half a year of continuous use I can safely say my Warmies sea turtle has held up well with no damage. The only change has been the fluff flattening out a bit on the belly, which should be expected. As someone with circulatory issues who suffers during colder months and gets plenty of use out of Shelby even when it's hot, I'm really really happy with my purchase!

product_name: Nooelec GOES Weather Satellite RTL-SDR Bundle - Includes NESDR SMArTee XTR Software Defined Radio, & Everything Else Needed to Receive LRIT, HRIT & HRPT Satellite Weather Images Directly from Space!
review_header: Put in the work... Get the GOES Goodies!
review_text: This is not a quickie project, be prepared to tinker. It is pretty cool though. 1. For a permanent install, you will NEED an SMA lightning arrestor, ground wire, and ground rod - unless you like the idea of bringing Thor into your house... I used this one from Amazon (CAREFUL, SMA is fragile to too much abuse!): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07K25Y1JW 2. For the Sawbird LNA, you will need a waterproof housing. I purchased this one off Amazon, and some 1-3/8 conduit straps which screwed directly to the back with the included screws (My antenna mast is chain link top-rail, 1-3/8" galvanized steel): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07RPNWD47. The Sawbird and the Lightning arrestor BARELY fit inside - had to finagle the cable glands to get it to work. 3. For the cable glands on that box, it was necessary to bore out the glands to 9/16" to fit the substantial cable ends that come on the LM400 cable included. Once that was done, they fit perfectly. That cable is robust, but the connectors are fragile. USE CABLE TIES! Torquing the cable will break SMA connectors. Just the weight of that cable might... 4. DO NOT USE A PHONE to locate the satellite, use a real high quality lensatic compass and the info from Dishpointer. With my phone, and Satellite Director 2.6.4, I was about 5 degrees off on the azimuth, so much so that it gave me bad signal-to-noise. Once I re-set the azimuth with my lensensatic compass, I got real images and data-dumps. About doubled my SNR (signat-to-noise). 5. I used a plumb-bob on a protractor to set the elevation, but "Clinometer" app on my Android phone was easier and gave decimal degrees. Held the phone against the LNB boom. 6. Skew sucks. My location called for 30.1 degrees - all you get is horizontal, 45, and 90. I picked 45 because it is closest, but the mount REALLY should be redesigned!!! I have it installed on my PC running ZorinOS 17.2 (Ubuntu fork) - Satdump was ok to install - nothing too crazy but Linux dependencies are always an issue. I used "DeepAI" to tell me what the error messages meant, and how to resolve them. Take it slow, Google is your friend. Tinker. I am happy!

review_header: It detects motion - BUT notifications of the motion are rarely sent to my phone.
review_text: This is the fourth manufacturer of a smart camera that is supposed to be able to tell Vehicles and humans apart from a bush blowing in the wind2,  or a pet or other animal walking in front of the camera.  Let me say first that NONE of the cameras are perfect for this purpose.  They all make mistakes from time to time.I am used to the imperfections in determining a vehicle or person - BUT what I cannot tolerate with this Reo-Link camera is that I rarely ever get notified that the camera picked up motion.  Yes the camera is usually recording the motion although that is not 100% either,  but even though the camera is on the latest version,  and I have reset the camera multiple times,  and saved the settings for notification both on and off numerous times I am rarely ever notified when motion is detected.There is even a 'Test send notifications' function but that has never worked.  I can accept that there is a LAG between the motion being captured and me being notified, since the data has to hit the cell tower first,  but what I CANNOT accept is that I never get ANY notification of movement most of the time.  This is the primary reason I wanted a camera at my gate so I would KNOW when someone is down at my gate.I do not think I will be keeping this camera.  Yes it is great that there are two cameras in one - but the fact that it is more expensive than many other cameras,  AND the fact that this REOLINK is not the critical function of NOTIFING me when movement is detected makes it extremely disappointing for me.I think I will invest in getting a POE cable down to the gate which will be expensive but it will give me a wider range of cameras to choose from. product_name: The Cut Buddy PLUS Beard Shaping Tool, Clear Template with Built-in Comb and Bonus Pencil, Ideal for Hairline, Beard, and Mustache Trimming
review_text:
Great idea in theory, practically useless for what I bought it for!





In theory, this product is fantastic. In practical application, however, it is absolutely terrible if you are trying to use it to create a clean front hairline on yourself.





The biggest problem is the complete lack of useful instructions for doing exactly that. The company repeatedly promotes this product as a tool for achieving a “sharp, perfect line” and even specifically advertises precise hairline shaping and professional line-ups. Yet I could not find a single video or clear set of instructions from the company showing or explaining how to actually use it to establish a front hairline on yourself.





There are countless videos and examples showing how to use this tool for shaping a beard, but apparently showing customers how to accomplish one of the other things the product is specifically advertised to do was not considered important.





That is incredibly frustrating. If you are going to repeatedly advertise a product as being capable of producing a precise, professional hairline, then show the customer how to use it for that purpose. Don't make a big deal out of everything the product supposedly does and then provide endless demonstrations for one use while completely ignoring another.





The tool itself may be perfectly adequate for beard shaping, but that doesn't help much when the reason you bought it was to create a clean front hairline and there is virtually no guidance on how to do that.





For the price, I expected a lot more—not necessarily a better piece of plastic, but **better information and instruction from the company selling it





Unfortunately, despite the low price, I cannot recommend this product for anyone buying it specifically to help create their own front hairline. The marketing makes it sound much more useful for that purpose than the actual support provided by the company.

product_name: Curt Manufacturing 18110 Cargo Carrier with 1-1/4" Fixed Shank
review_text:
I purchased this cargo carrier for my 2006 Honda CR-V.  I'm glad I did.  The carrier cleared both the mounted spare tire and the exhaust flow.  I think a carrier without the rise from the hitch receptacle would have hot exhaust blowing on the cargo.  On my way east (empty) from California, I stopped at multiple rock collecting sites.  Several were rough enough to actually drag the carrier.  Yes, I need to do a little sanding and repainting.  But the terrain did not cause any structural damage, as I would have experienced by a carrier positioned a few inches lower.


Interestingly, in Colorado I accidentally left a small stone unsecured in the carrier.  I found it when I reached my destination in Michigan.  That tells me it's a smooth ride back there.


I loaded the carrier with multiple plastic bins of various sizes, secured with straps.  The return trip included midwestern storms, snow closure of I-80 in Wyoming and choking smoke in California's central valley.  Everything arrived in the same condition it was packed.


Importantly, I noticed no difference in handling or fuel consumption.  That's the reason I chose a hitch mounted carrier over one attached to my roof rack.


Oh, it probably took me an hour to assemble.  I'm sure I could have done it faster if I had done it on a work bench in my shop, instead of working at foot level on my deck.  It was pretty easy and straight forward.  Reflective tape on the corners is a good suggestion.


Update:  While considering this purchase, the geometry of the shank was of interest to me.  I read what I could, rolled the dice, and got the results I needed.  Please check my newly added photos.  You'll see the tray sits 11.5 inches back from the center of the hitch pin hole.  The rise of the shank is 2 inches.  Hope this helps you.

product_name: You Are Fatally Invited: The twistiest mystery thriller of 2025, perfect for fans of Agatha Christie and 'The Guest List'
review_text: As soon as I spotted this book, I just knew I had to read it!With a front cover and title that just screams murder, I couldn't wait to dive right in.I absolutely love a locked room murder mystery and this totally gave me Knives Out vibes (or going back to books, Christie vibes)With all our suspects gathered on Alastor's private Island, one dead guest creates the most realistic thriller retreat ever.The story unfolds gradually as we meet each character through their own pov chapters.I love this format as it really helps us to see into their minds and get a clear view of who they are and what each of them are thinking about each other....and the murder at hand.However, whether we always get an authentic and reliable narrative is up to us to determine.This was pretty easy to navigate with only a few characters and each chapter is clearly marked - but as more information is revealed, it gets trickier to keep track of how each of the connections develop and this had me not trusting anyone there.This was a brilliantly worked plot, packed with clues and twists to keep you guessing right to the end.I was completely hooked from the start and by the second half, I just couldn't put this down and had to stay up late to see how it all played out in the end.One of my favourite genres and done to perfection! I loved this and can't wait to see more from this author in the future.

product_name: Nugget Ice Maker Countertop - Silonn Pebble Ice Maker Machine Crushed Ice, Pellet Ice 44 lbs per Day, Pull-Out Water Tank and Removable Ice Basket for Home, Kitchen, Stainless Steel
review_header: Just In Time Ice -- Small Nugget Size
review_text: The ice maker in my fridge froze up enough times that I just turned it off and either bought ice or (infrequently) used ice trays. No more ice buying for me! Fill up the tray with a bottle of water (it holds just under 2 quarts) and the first nuggets start popping out after 10 minutes. It will continue to spawn ice for another 90 minutes or so, after which it turns off. It does not appear to have a cooling mechanism for the actual ice tray, so they will start to melt. This ice really is for immediate use. I moved a tray over into the freezer and they all kind of gummed up, so that's probably not worth it. The ice comes out as 1/2 inch cubed nuggets -- the kind you might find at a sonic drive through. They are soft-ish, so not as bad for your teeth as other ice cubes and quickly cools off your drink, but also melts quite quickly. Half way to crushed ice, but not quite It is a bit expensive and I have not had a chance to compare either quality or productivity with some of the cheaper models. That said, I am quite happy with it and therefore unlikely to try one of the cheaper models. This model seems quite solid and well-built.

This means that when you accidentally hit one of your teeth with the back while brushing, it is more jarring and makes a much louder sound. The bristles are not as “sturdy” as the original brush heads. They do the job, they are still very usable, but I can see them not lasting as long as the original heads. The bottom where you attach the head to the brush is soft plastic and it’s somewhat easy to malform it if you miss the hole when trying to attach it. If the plastic around the hole gets bent or deformed in any way, the head will no longer fit to the base and it will make a terrible rattling noise when you use it. Overall, these are not bad at all. They fall a bit short when compared to the OEM heads, but they are also reasonably less expensive.
